[#hash-macs-choose]
.How to choose among "Message authentication"
[cols="2,2,2,4,4",options="header"]
|===
| Name | Fastest natively | Smallest on Emscripten | Where it is used | Choose it when

| <<hash-siphash,`siphash_32`>>
| 1,624 MiB/s (hash2)
| 6,206 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://docs.kernel.org/security/siphash.html[the Linux kernel's hsiphash]
| Hash tables on 32-bit targets whose keys an adversary chooses.

| <<hash-siphash,`siphash_64`>>
| 3,274 MiB/s (hash2)
| 6,294 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://peps.python.org/pep-0456/[Python's string hashing (PEP 456)]; link:https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/collections/struct.HashMap.html[Rust's default HashMap hasher]
| Every hash table, set or Bloom filter whose keys come from the network or another user.

| <<hash-mac-family,`macs::siphash_2_4`>>
| -
| -
| link:https://peps.python.org/pep-0456/[Python's string hashing (PEP 456)]
| To compute it in one call, on a backend named in the call; siphash_64 itself for hash_append and a hash table's hasher.

| <<hash-kmac,`macs::kmac_128`>>
| -
| -
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-56Cr2[A MAC and a KDF of NIST SP 800-56C (KMAC-based key derivation)]
| Where a standard or a format names KMAC; HMAC-SHA-256 elsewhere, which every platform has.

| <<hash-kmac,`macs::kmac_256`>>
| -
| -
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-56Cr2[A MAC and a KDF of NIST SP 800-56C (KMAC-based key derivation)]
| As KMAC128, where a format asks for 256-bit security.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac`>>
| 599 MiB/s (hash2)
| 14,437 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2104[RFC 2104]
| HMAC over a hash that has no alias of its own.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_md5_128`>>
| 932 MiB/s (hash2)
| 8,330 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6151#section-2.3[RFC 6151 on HMAC-MD5]
| Only for an existing protocol.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_sha1_160`>>
| 1,185 MiB/s (hash2)
| 10,569 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6238[TOTP and HOTP codes (RFC 6238, RFC 4226)]
| Only for an existing protocol, such as authenticator-app codes.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_sha2_224`>>
| 582 MiB/s (hash2)
| 14,444 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4231[RFC 4231's test cases]
| When a standard asks for it.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_sha2_256`>>
| 582 MiB/s (hash2)
| 14,437 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7518#section-3.2[JSON Web Tokens signed HS256]; link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#section-7.1[TLS 1.3's HKDF]
| The default MAC: interoperable, in every browser.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_sha2_384`>>
| 911 MiB/s (hash2)
| 17,975 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7518#section-3.2[JSON Web Tokens signed HS384]
| When a standard asks for it.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_sha2_512`>>
| 930 MiB/s (hash2)
| 17,980 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0032.mediawiki[BIP32's key derivation]; link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7518#section-3.2[JSON Web Tokens signed HS512]
| When a standard asks for it, or for a 512-bit tag.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_sha2_512_224`>>
| 939 MiB/s (hash2)
| 18,041 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.180-4[FIPS 180-4's truncated SHA-512]
| When a standard asks for it.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_sha2_512_256`>>
| 904 MiB/s (hash2)
| 17,992 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.180-4[FIPS 180-4's truncated SHA-512; not libsodium's crypto_auth, which truncates HMAC-SHA-512's tag]
| When a standard asks for it.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_sha3_224`>>
| 733 MiB/s (hash2)
| 7,427 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.202[FIPS 202]
| When a standard asks for it.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_sha3_256`>>
| 686 MiB/s (hash2)
| 7,416 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.202[FIPS 202]
| When a standard asks for it.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_sha3_384`>>
| 526 MiB/s (hash2)
| 7,383 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.202[FIPS 202]
| When a standard asks for it.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_sha3_512`>>
| 366 MiB/s (hash2)
| 7,386 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.202[FIPS 202]
| When a standard asks for it.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_ripemd_128`>>
| 959 MiB/s (hash2)
| 9,712 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2286[RFC 2286's test cases]
| Only for an existing protocol.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_ripemd_160`>>
| 607 MiB/s (hash2)
| 11,897 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2286[RFC 2286's test cases]
| Only for an existing protocol.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_blake2b_512`>>
| 1,548 MiB/s (hash2)
| 12,262 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7693#section-2.5[RFC 7693, whose keyed mode makes HMAC unnecessary]
| When a protocol names HMAC-BLAKE2b; otherwise a keyed blake2b_512.

| <<hash-hmac,`hmac_blake2s_256`>>
| 922 MiB/s (hash2)
| 11,284 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.wireguard.com/protocol/[WireGuard's HKDF]
| For WireGuard-style protocols.

| -
| -
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6151#section-2.3[RFC 6151 on HMAC-MD5]

The measured columns are doc/measurements.json's, a reference measured on 2026-11-16 on Apple M5 Max that decides nothing: the native throughput over 1 MiB, or the time of one derivation over `hmac_sha2_256`, of the fastest backend, and the smallest Emscripten program that calls the function; <<hash-measurements>> has every backend on every target.
